question:
Consider the following:

1) Bank rate

2) Income tax rates

3) Repo rates

4) Reverse repo rate

Which of these rates is/are decided by the Reserve Bank of India?
solution:
The correct answer is **Only 1, 3 and 4.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bank Rate**

 
 
• ​The Reserve Bank of India** (RBI) lends money **to commercial banks at the bank rate without **requiring any collateral**.
 
• A commercial bank's borrowing costs rise when the central bank raises the Bank Rate, which **reduces the market's supply** of money.
 
• The Bank Rate is **4.25 percent as of March 2021.**
 
 
 
• **Repo Rates**
 
 
• The rate at which the central bank (RBI) lends money to commercial banks to meet **short-term fund requirements** in order to maintain liquidity and control inflation is known as the repo rate or **repurchase rate.**
 
• The** Monetary policy committee** (MPC), which is led by the governor of the **RBI**, decides the repo rate.
 
• According to the most recent update from the Reserve Bank of India, which will take effect in** August 2021,** the repo rate in India is currently **4%**.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rates**
 
 
• The term "reverse repo rate" refers to the interest rate at which the Indian central bank, or RBI, **borrows money** from commercial banks for a brief period of time.
 
• The economy is impacted by the reverse repo rate because banks deposit their **surplus funds** with the RBI to earn interest when the reverse repo rate rises.
 
• The RBI will set the reverse repo rate at **3.35 percent in August 2021.​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India became a member bank of the **Asian Clearing Union** after it was **nationalized in 1949.**
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is a **national institution **and the foundation of the expanding** Indian economy**. The **International Monetary Fund (IMF) **counts it among its members.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar's strategies in his book** "The Problem of the Rupee – Its Origin and its Solution" **served as the foundation for the Reserve Bank of India's concept.
 
 

c1
